question: Why did Swiss Emmental develop fewer and fewer holes over recent decades?
answer: Because milk got cleaner. The holes form when carbon dioxide made by propionic bacteria gathers around tiny particles, and a 2015 Agroscope study found that microscopic hay dust in the milk was doing that job. Closed modern milking systems keep hay out, so the gas had fewer places to start. Adding measured hay powder brought the holes back.
move: When a result fades after a clean-up, suspect the dirt was doing something.
